# Facilitator Guide — AI Security for Builders

Slides: `slides/slides.md`. Demos: `demos/`. Exercise sheets: `exercises.md`. Every demo runs offline; start times assume 09:30.

**One week before:** run `python demos/run_all.py`. Confirm room, projector, one laptop per pair, Wi-Fi. Print exercises and handouts.

## Day 1

| Time | Segment | What you do and say |
|---|---|---|
| 09:30 | Welcome | Outcomes on the first slide. Ask each table for the one question they want answered; write them on the flipchart. |
| 09:40 | **Module 1 — Threat model** | Teach: OWASP LLM Top 10, injection, data poisoning, exfiltration, denial of wallet. |
| 10:27 | Demo 1 | **Run `python demos/01_threat_model.py`** — a system described as components and data flows, mapped to LLM-specific threats with likelihood × impact scoring and the control that addresses each. Close with: *“Anywhere untrusted text can reach your prompt is an input field for the attacker. Draw those arrows first.”* |
| 10:52 | Lab 1 | Threat model your system — see `exercises.md`. Walk the room; collect one result per table. |

Close with: *“No single control stops everything. Defence in depth means each attack has to get lucky five times.”* |
| 13:49 | **Module 2 — Controls** (2/2) | Teach: output handling, guardrail classifiers, ACL defence in depth. |

| 15:40 | Break |  |

Close with: *“You will never enumerate every prompt. Make sure the tool refuses the refund even when the model has been convinced.”* |
| 17:07 | Day close | Each table: one thing they will use tomorrow. Homework: bring one real example for the next lab. |

## If short on time

Keep every demo; shorten the teaching before it. Cut labs to a paired discussion of the lab question rather than dropping them. Never cut the close.

## What can go wrong

- **A demo fails on the day** — you ran `run_all.py` last week, so it is the environment: `pip install -r requirements.txt`, then re-run. Screenshots of each output live in nobody's folder: take them after your dry run.
- **No projector / terminal too small** — open `/demos` in a browser and run the same demo from the *Course labs* section.
- **The room has no laptops** — run labs as table discussions using the printed exercise sheet; you run the script and change the inputs they call out.
